title: Far-pair offset collimation under collective weight dephasing

claims.statement: For every integer N >= 2 and every s modulo N, the collective-weight far-pair designated-offset algorithm in proof.md, with n=ceil(log2 N), its public integer schedule and two deterministic budgets, and its finite-length fallback, recovers the entire s with unconditional probability greater than 0.98 under the collective-weight source model in proof.md, including independent ideal copies. The same configuration jointly has branchwise charged sequential work O(2^((9/8) sqrt(n log2 n) + sqrt(n))), with exact growth index 1/2.

structured.error_model: Collective weight-controlled isometry source. With n=ceil(log2 N), consecutive blocks have exactly 8*m_1 usual raw (n+1)-qubit registers on the main branch, where m_1 is the public first transition width in proof.md. Fallback blocks have two registers. At the start of each block the provider forms fresh mutually independent ideal coset states of the fixed s, independent of its private memory and existing solver registers. Before emitting the block it applies an isometry sum_w Pi_w tensor V_w, with Pi_w the total branch-qubit Hamming-weight projector of the block and V_w any isometry on its private memory into a common output space. It acts as identity on all position registers. The provider emits the resulting systems sequentially and cannot alter that action within the block. It may use earlier classical outcomes and memory, including memory correlated with earlier blocks, to choose the next isometries. It never accesses previously emitted systems or future private solver randomness. The algorithm sees no flags. Up to floor(epsilon(n) Q) of the acquired copies may be affected by this channel, including all Q for epsilon(n)=1. This includes independent ideal copies by using identical isometries at all weights. No guarantee is asserted for channels outside this promise.
